hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? does your mind ever talk to you at two in the morning?
options: then this one is for you. listen.
most people know that voice. listen.
lucky you. you’ll still recognize it.

steps.line: In the garden, with everything given and one tree held back, someone began to talk. Not with a shout. With a whisper.
“Then Shaytan whispered to them,” the Qur’an says. The Arabic is waswasa. Say it slowly: was-was. The word itself whispers.

steps.q: What do you think the whisper said?
steps.why: He didn’t say disobey. He renamed it the tree of eternity, and promised a kingdom that never decays (Qur’an 20:120).

steps.line: He didn’t say “disobey God.” He renamed the tree: the tree of forever, a kingdom that never wears out. And he swore he was their sincere adviser.

steps.q: Why rename the tree, instead of just saying “disobey”?
o: A wrong thing dressed as a gift is easy to take
He didn’t know what the tree really was
Because God had never told them its name
steps.why: Nobody reaches for “disobey.” Plenty reach for “forever.”

steps.q: In the Qur’an, why did Shaytan (Iblis) turn against Adam in the first place?
o: He was too proud to bow to Adam
Adam had tricked him out of the garden
He wanted the tree for himself
steps.why: Iblis said, “I am better than him: You made me from fire and him from clay” (7:12). Pride first, then the whisper.

steps.line: They both ate. At once they saw their nakedness, and began covering themselves with leaves of the garden.
Today, at two in the morning, a voice starts up. Reasonable. One more episode. Or: you’ll never be good enough. It sounds exactly like you.
steps.label: today

steps.line: Companions once told the Prophet ﷺ of thoughts too awful to say out loud. “You really find that?” he asked. “That is clear faith.”

steps.q: The Qur’an’s last surah asks refuge from the whisperer who… what?
o: Slinks back when God is remembered
steps.why: Surah an-Nas calls him al-waswas al-khannas: the whisperer who withdraws. Early commentators said he pulls back whenever God is remembered. Many Muslims recite it before sleep.

say: here’s what i love. the qur’an says they both ate. no one blames the woman alone. and the story names the whisper, so you can name it too.
in islam, a passing thought isn’t a sin. a saying teaches that God forgives what crosses the mind, unless you act on it or say it.

steps.q: The companions were horrified by their own thoughts, and he called that horror “clear faith.” What does that tell you?
o: A dark thought means faith is gone
Hating the thought shows it isn’t you
Dark thoughts must be confessed aloud
steps.why: Hating the whisper is the proof it isn’t yours. Not every voice in your head is you.

today.say: today, when a nagging voice starts up, ask it one question: is that mine? if you like, say the short refuge many muslims use: a‘udhu billah, i seek refuge in God. or listen to an-nas, the last surah, about the whisperer.
options: lovely. not every voice is yours.
beautiful. a few words, very old, very calm.

sources: Qur’an 7:20-22 (“Then Satan whispered to them… Your Lord forbade you from this tree only lest ye should become angels or become of the immortals. And he swore unto them: Lo! I am a sincere adviser… they began to hide (by heaping) on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden,” Pickthall)
Qur’an 20:120 (“Shall I show thee the tree of immortality and power that wasteth not away?”)
Sahih Muslim 132 (companions found in themselves thoughts too grave to speak; “Do you really find that?” “Yes.” “That is clear faith”)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5269; Sahih Muslim 127 (Allah has forgiven my community what their souls whisper, as long as they do not act on it or speak it)
